title: Bulacan Marathon 2026: A Half-Marathon Hit Goes the Full 42K
seo_title: Bulacan Marathon 2026 Review: SM Center Pulilan
meta_description: Team Malofit's first full marathon lands at SM Center Pulilan on Aug 9, 2026, built on a sold-out half-marathon legacy. Here's what to know before entering.
dek: The organizers behind Bulacan's crowd-pleasing half marathon are stretching to 42.195km for the first time, bringing their proven medal-and-string-bag playbook to a brand-new full-marathon debut in Pulilan.
verdict: This is an untested full marathon from a team with a genuinely good half-marathon track record, not the other way around. If you want a low-key, well-stocked provincial debut with generous entitlements and a community that has shown up before, it's a reasonable bet. If you need a certified course, published elevation profile, or hard cutoff-time data before committing to 42.195km, that information simply isn't public yet, so go in treating this as a first-edition leap of faith rather than a known quantity.

sections.heading: From Half to Full: A First-Time Leap
paragraphs: The Bulacan Marathon 2026 marks the first time this organizing team has staged a full 42.195km race, framed explicitly as a step up from their existing half-marathon franchise after "the success of the Bulacan Half Marathon and due to insistent demand from the running community" [1]. Team Malofit x Pairfect Fit are the same duo behind that half-marathon series, now extending it into 42K, 21K, 10K and 5K categories on August 9, 2026 [1][2].

The race hub sits at SM Center, Pulilan, Bulacan, a shift from the Waltermart Plaridel base used by the half-marathon side of the franchise [2]. For a debut full marathon, that's a meaningful change of scenery, and it means runners who've done the half in past years shouldn't assume the 42K retraces exactly the same roads.

sections.heading: What the Course Precedent Suggests
paragraphs: Public listings for the 2026 Bulacan Marathon don't yet spell out a detailed 42K route map, elevation profile, or road-closure plan. What is available is the organizer's half-marathon precedent: in past editions, 21K runners went out from the Waltermart hub, traversed Plaridel-Bustos Road, made a U-turn at San Pedro Bustos, and returned to the start [4].

That's the kind of flat, out-and-back provincial road course that's typical of Bulacan's running scene, but it's important to be clear this describes the half-marathon's established route, not a confirmed map for the new full-marathon distance. Anyone targeting a marathon PR or Boston-style qualifying time should hold off on assumptions until the organizer publishes specific 42K course details.

sections.heading: Organisation, Pricing and Entitlements
paragraphs: Registration is tiered by distance: the pricing structure and race-day inclusions cover a race bib with time chip, a full-sublimation singlet, a finisher shirt, a finisher medal that scales up with distance, and a string bag across all four categories [2][3]. Medal sizes step up from 4 inches for the 10K and 5K to 5.5 inches for the 21K and 6.5 inches for the marathon itself [3].

There's a built-in incentive to sign up early: the first 1,000 42K registrants and the first 1,500 21K registrants are promised exclusive "BM Vamos Socks" as a bonus on top of the standard kit [3]. Registration runs both online and in person, with walk-in sign-ups handled through Pairfect Fit's location on Plaridel Diversion Road, in front of Waltermart, Monday through Saturday from 10am to 6pm [3].

sections.heading: Atmosphere and Track Record
paragraphs: The half-marathon side of this franchise has a genuine track record worth noting: the 2020 edition sold out and rewarded finishers with what was, at the time, a standout 5-inch medal [4]. The 2025 edition was described as building on "highly successful" past turnout, again featuring a sold-out crowd [5].

Marketing for the most recent half-marathon edition leans into a festive, community feel, with organizers touting a course that "winds through Plaridel's key roads and is known for its festive vibe, generous inclusions, and fun-filled hydration stations" [6]. That local-pride, well-supported-aid-station energy is presumably the template the team is trying to carry into the new marathon distance, though a debut 42K field will inevitably feel different from a well-worn half-marathon course.

sections.heading: Should You Run It?
paragraphs: If you're chasing the novelty of an inaugural marathon medal, want a budget-friendly provincial race with decently generous entitlements, and don't mind some first-year unknowns around course specifics, the Bulacan Marathon 2026 is worth a look, especially given the organizer's demonstrated ability to sell out half-marathon fields and deliver on entitlements in past years [4][5]. It's a sensible pick for runners based in or near Bulacan who already trust this organizing team from the half-marathon series.

If you're traveling specifically for a certified marathon time, need published cutoff and elevation data before committing, or want a big-city marathon atmosphere, this may not be the right fit yet, simply because that level of detail hasn't been made public for the 42K category [2]. Given the sock-perk cap on the first 1,000 marathon entrants and the franchise's history of selling out, registering early is the practical move either way [1][3][4].

faqs.question: When and where is the Bulacan Marathon 2026?
faqs.answer: It's set for August 9, 2026, with the race hub at SM Center, Pulilan, Bulacan, and offers four distances: 42K, 21K, 10K, and 5K [2]. This is a new venue compared to the organizer's half-marathon series, which has been based at Waltermart Plaridel [2].

faqs.question: Is this the same organizer as the Bulacan Half Marathon?
faqs.answer: Yes. Team Malofit x Pairfect Fit, who run the established Bulacan Half Marathon, are launching the full marathon as an expansion "due to insistent demand from the running community" [1]. It's their first time staging the 42.195km distance [1].

faqs.question: What do runners get for their registration fee?
faqs.answer: Every category includes a race bib with time chip, a sublimated singlet, a finisher shirt, a finisher medal (sized up to 6.5 inches for the 42K), and a string bag [2][3]. The first 1,000 42K and first 1,500 21K registrants also get exclusive BM Vamos Socks [3].

faqs.question: Where can I register in person?
faqs.answer: Walk-in registration is available at Pairfect Fit on Plaridel Diversion Road, in front of Waltermart, Monday to Saturday from 10am to 6pm [3]. Online registration is also open through the event's official listing [2].
